description:
## Why

PKIX-xj81 decomposition, pattern 2 of 6. Key-rollover topology: a trust anchor
rotates its signing key; the old TA self-signs a cross-cert that asserts the
new TA. End-entity certs signed by the new key must validate through the
cross-cert when the verifier only knows the old key as anchor.

## What

Pool topology:

```
OldRootSelf  (TA, SKI=oldkey, signs with oldkey)
NewRootCross (subject=NewRoot, issued by OldRoot, signed with oldkey,
              SPKI=newkey)
RolloverEE   (signed with newkey, AKI=newkey)
```

Build steps:

1. Generator issues:
   - `OldRootSelf.crt` (anchor, self-signed with oldkey).
   - `NewRootCross.crt` (issued by OldRoot, signed with oldkey, subject DN
     same as NewRoot, SPKI = newkey).
   - `RolloverEE.crt` (signed by newkey, AKI keyIdentifier = newkey SKI).
2. Test (`tests/key_rollover.rs`):
   - Anchor list: `[OldRootSelf]`.
   - Pool: `[NewRootCross]`.
   - `build_path(&ee, &pool, &anchors)` must succeed and return a chain
     ending at NewRootCross, with the verifier walking via oldkey to
     anchor OldRootSelf.
   - `validate_path(...)` must succeed.
3. Oracle: cert SKIs / AKIs extracted by hard-coded hex literals captured
   from `openssl x509 -text` at fixture-creation time, compared independently
   of the path builder.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Three DER fixtures committed.
- [ ] Generation reproducible via `generate.sh`.
- [ ] One integration test verifying the rollover path is found and
      validated.

## Depends on

PKIX-xj81.1 (shared generator + helpers).
